summary.headline: Sharda Cropchem Q1 FY27 revenue rose 9% to Rs.1,074 crore and EBITDA 25% to Rs.178 crore, but reported PAT of Rs.88 crore was cushioned by lower forex gains.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 9% YoY to Rs.1,074 crore, with volume down 1.6% and forex contributing 12.7 points. EBITDA margin expanded 220 bps to 16.6% and gross margin rose 120 bps to 36.7%, driven by mix in NAFTA, LATAM and rest of world. Europe revenue softened as distributors cut stock after an unusual heatwave, though Europe gross margin improved to 44.2%. Forex gain fell to Rs.7.5 crore from Rs.73.1 crore, so reported PBT and PAT looked weaker, while management said PBT before forex grew 16% to Rs.111 crore. Management maintained FY27 guidance of 10-15% revenue growth and about 35% gross margin.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Largest market; revenue softened as distributors cut stock after heatwave. Gross margin 44.2% vs 42.9% in Q1 FY26. Management said restocking has largely normalised.

segments.name: NAFTA
segments.commentary: Gross margin 32.8% vs 25.9% a year ago; growth strong and margins improved this quarter.

segments.name: LATAM
segments.commentary: Among the strongest growth engines this quarter, but gross margin fell to 16.9% from 28.0% a year ago.

segments.name: Rest of world
segments.commentary: Gross margin 30.8% vs 26.8% in Q1 FY26; growth reported as good with better profitability.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 10-15% maintained; volume growth expected at about 5-10%.
FY27 gross margin guided at 35% to 37% (management, in Q&A), and EBITDA margin in the 18-20% range.
Effective tax rate on annualised basis expected at 18-20%, with Q1 running higher.
Amortisation expected to be about Rs.370-375 crore annualised for FY27 vs about Rs.325 crore last year.
Management expects Europe volumes to recover to prior-year levels and the next three quarters to be better than Q1; last month of Q2 said to be better than Q1.
Registration investment of about Rs.450-500 crore per year; FY27 spend to rise further.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex was Rs.273 crore against FY27 guidance of Rs.500 crore; management says guidance not revised and the year could be Rs.480-550 crore.
Q1 capex was elevated by heavy data compensation payments, which management says will not repeat.
Total product registrations at 30 June 2026 were 3,016 (3,011 at 31 March 2026), with 1,027 applications pending.
Registrations by region: Europe 1,682 (up 3), NAFTA 325 (up 2), LATAM 760 (flat), rest of world 249 (flat).
demand_pricing: Volume declined 1.6% YoY; forex added 12.7 points and product mix subtracted 2.1 points.
Management said prices are improving sequentially after a severe decline about two years ago.
Europe revenue fell on distributor destocking linked to heatwave; management attributes this to weather, not molecules.
LATAM and NAFTA growth may partly reflect customer pre-buying ahead of season, per analyst; management said there is no strong trend.
Sourcing is 100% contract manufacturing, mainly from China, and all purchases are in US dollars.

qa_highlights.question: Split of the 9% revenue growth into volume, forex and realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume -1.6%, forex +12.7%, product mix -2.1%, total +9%. Management said the mix impact is concentrated in Europe and should improve next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Rs.7.5 crore forex gain and its accounting?
qa_highlights.answer: It is mainly unrealised, from repricing foreign-currency receivables and payables at each balance sheet date. Q1 FY26 had a Rs.73 crore unrealised gain from a roughly 10% EUR/USD move. EBITDA excludes forex.

qa_highlights.question: Has Europe restocking normalised and what is FY27 EBITDA margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said restocking has improved and is largely normal, and guided FY27 EBITDA margin to 18-20%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is capex Rs.273 crore in Q1 vs Rs.500 crore guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance not revised; Q1 included heavy data compensation spend that is not expected to recur. Full year could be Rs.480-550 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company report PAT excluding forex for like-to-like comparison?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO pointed to the investor presentation, which gives PBT and EBIT excluding forex. He said more clarity will be provided in future presentations.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the NAFTA and LATAM gross margin, and do margins hold for the rest of the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Europe mix and price increases drove margins, LATAM volumes grew but margins dipped, and it expects Europe and NAFTA margins to stay in the same range.

risks_watch: Pace of Europe volume recovery after distributor destocking; management guides to a better next three quarters but gave no quantified timing.
LATAM gross margin fell to 16.9% from 28.0% despite strong volume growth.
Forex volatility: EUR/USD near 1.14 vs about 1.16-1.17 last year; management said it cannot be predicted.
Amortisation rising to about Rs.370-375 crore annualised, which pressures reported profit.
Registration pace: about 100 new registrations over three years versus about 300 in FY21-23, per analyst; no FY27 registration target given.
Capex range wide (Rs.480-550 crore) with no firm guidance revision.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the full-year outlook and on Europe recovery, but evasive on forex reporting, the capex range and the drivers of regional margins, which management called too detailed for the call. Management often deflected to weather and uncertainty.
key_quotes: It has improved and has reached to normal. In most of the cases, it is reaching the normality.
We don't manufacture anything anywhere in the world, including India.
So, on annualized basis, could be around Rs. 370-375 crores.
